title: VESPER SecuritySignal
description: IC-009. The typed security event A-044 asserts detection emits. The registry calls this the highest-value of the seven remaining depth gaps, and the reason is asymmetry: ADR-007 D6 supplies the compromise-RESPONSE half in full, while the DETECTION half had no artifact -- so a response mechanism sat behind a trigger nobody had typed. The triage rule distinguishing anomaly from indicator from incident is DF-SECURITY-TRIAGE, and the scope is fixed by OWNER-DECISION-005: owner-enrolled assets only, a target outside the enrolled set is REFUSED rather than scanned. Authority: SR-038, ARCH-19, IC-009, A-044, INV-TRUST-1, ADR-007 D6, OWNER-DECISION-005; REM-011.

asset_ref.description: The subject asset. Always present: a security signal with no subject cannot be triaged and cannot be scoped.

enrolment.description: OWNER-DECISION-005's permanent scope, checked BEFORE classification rather than after. Confirmed by the owner 2026-08-12 (single-occupant dwelling, no third-party assets in range). Placing this block ahead of `classification` is deliberate: a signal about an unenrolled asset must never acquire a severity, because a severity is what justifies a response against it.

scope_decision.description: REFUSED_UNENROLLED is emitted and logged rather than dropped. A silently discarded out-of-scope signal is indistinguishable from a detector that was never running -- and 'I could not check it' must never read the same as 'it passed'.

classification.description: The output of DF-SECURITY-TRIAGE. The three-way split is the whole point: an anomaly is a deviation, an indicator is a deviation with a known attack signature, an incident is an indicator with confirmed effect. Collapsing them produces either alarm fatigue or a missed intrusion, and which one depends only on where the single threshold was set.

confidence.description: Null is legal and means unquantified. INV-EVID-3: UNKNOWN is first-class, and a fabricated 0.5 is worse than an honest null because it is arithmetically usable.

basis.description: What the classification rests on: the rule ids or signature ids that fired. minItems 1 -- a classification with no basis is a verdict with no evidence, which INV-EVID-1 forbids emitting as an assertion.

evidence.description: A-044: 'evidence is preserved BEFORE remediation'. Ordering is the assertion, so it is a field rather than a hope. Isolating a node destroys volatile state; a remediation that ran first is a remediation that destroyed the record of what it was remediating.

preserved_before_remediation.description: FALSE is a recorded failure of the procedure, not a configuration. It exists so the violation is visible in the log rather than absent from it.

response.description: ADR-007 D6's half, bound to the detection half by the same envelope. INV-TRUST-1 is the constraint that makes isolation meaningful: a node demoted to Z2 may not hold state, issue commands or receive secrets, so isolation is a trust-zone transition rather than a firewall rule.
